title: Immunofluorescence microscopy-based assessment of cytosolic DNA accumulation in mammalian cells
protocol: Detach TS/A cells from maintenance cultures in T75 flasks.
Discard exhausted culture medium.
Add 2 mL 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA to each flask.
Incubate flasks for 2–3 min at 37°C.
Collect detached cells in 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 350 g, 20°C–25°C for 5 min.
Discard supernatants.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL complete culture medium.
Count cells with a standard or automated hemocytometer.
Add complete culture medium to the cell suspension to achieve 1 × 10^4 cells/mL.
Seed 0.5 mL of this suspension in coverslip-containing 24-well plates and return plates to the incubator.
Replace exhausted culture medium with 0.5 mL fresh, pre-warmed complete culture medium.
Expose cells to a single irradiation dose of 8 Gy with a SARRP.
Discard culture medium.
Fix cells with 0.5 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (w/v in PBS) for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Wash fixed cells twice with 0.5 mL PBS.
Transfer coverslips to a fresh 24-well plate containing 0.5 mL PBS per well.
Discard PBS.
Permeabilize cells with 0.5 mL permeabilization buffer A for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Wash coverslips three times with 0.5 mL PBS.
Block unspecific binding sites with 0.5 mL blocking buffer for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Transfer coverslips sample-side onto microscopy slides or parafilm within an opaque humidified chamber containing ddH2O.
Stain cytosolic dsDNA by gently dropping 60 μL of blocking buffer supplemented with anti-dsDNA antibodies (1:1000 v/v) onto each coverslip.
Maintain coverslips in the humidified chamber for 12–16 h at 4°C.
Supplement blocking buffer with anti-dsDNA antibodies (1:1000 v/v) for staining.
Transfer coverslips to a new 24-well plate containing 0.5 mL washing buffer per well.
Wash coverslips three times (5 min each) with washing buffer.
Stain anti-dsDNA antibodies with 0.3 mL of blocking buffer supplemented with Alexa Fluor® 594-conjugated anti-mouse antibodies (1:1000 v/v) for 30–60 min at 20°C–25°C.
Optionally, supplement the blocking buffer with anti-COX4 (1:300 v/v).
Optionally, supplement the blocking buffer with anti-TFAM (1:500 v/v).
Supplement blocking buffer with Alexa Fluor® 488-conjugated anti-rabbit antibodies (1:1000 v/v) for simultaneous staining of COX4 or TFAM.
Wash coverslips three times (5 min each) with washing buffer.
Transfer coverslips to a new 24-well plate containing 0.5 mL washing buffer per well.
Wash coverslips once with 0.5 mL PBS.
Discard PBS.
Re-fix cells with 0.5 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Wash coverslips three times with 0.5 mL PBS.
Re-permeabilize cells with 0.5 mL permeabilization buffer B for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Wash coverslips three times with 0.5 mL PBS.
Block unspecific binding sites with 0.5 mL blocking buffer for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C.
Transfer coverslips sample-side onto microscopy slides or parafilm within an opaque humidified chamber containing ddH2O.
Mix up to three coverslips next to each other on the same slide.
Encircle each coverslip with a hydrophobic barrier from a PAP Pen.
Drop 60 μL of blocking buffer supplemented with anti-LMNB1 antibodies (1:500 v/v) onto each coverslip.
Maintain coverslips in the humidified chamber for 12–16 h at 4°C.
Discard the staining solution after primary staining.
Transfer coverslip to a new 24-well plate containing 0.5 mL washing buffer per well.
Wash coverslips three times (5 min each) with washing buffer.
Stain anti-LMNB1 antibodies with 0.3 mL of blocking buffer supplemented with Alexa Fluor® 488-conjugated anti-rabbit antibodies (1:1000 v/v) for 30-60 min at 20°C–25°C.
Wash coverslips three times (5 min each) with washing buffer.
Wash coverslips once with 0.5 mL PBS.
Place one drop of DAPI-containing mounting medium on a standard slide for microscopy.
Retrieve individual coverslips from 24-well plates with Graefe forceps and rapidly dry them on paper.
Lay coverslip sample-side down on the mounting medium drop so that stained cells are in direct contact with the medium.
Adjust laser power and gain of each channel to satisfy the dynamic range by imaging 2–3 control and 2–3 treated samples.
Image at least 3 representative fields from each sample on individual blue (DAPI), red (cytosolic dsDNA) and green (LMNB1, COX4 or TFAM) channels.
Adjust illumination power and exposure time of each channel to satisfy the dynamic range by imaging 2–3 control and 2–3 treated samples.
Select illumination power and exposure time to prevent overexposure of each fluorophore in the brightest condition.
Image at least 3 fields per coverslip on individual blue, red, and green channels.
Merge single-channel images for visualization or quantitative assessments using ImageJ/FIJI or widefield microscope software packages.
Process single-channel widefield microscopy images to assess the number of cytosolic dsDNA-positive foci in each cell.
Determine the percentage of cells containing cytosolic dsDNA-positive foci.
Analyze spatial localization of cytosolic dsDNA-positive foci with respect to COX4, TFAM, or LMNB1.
Open single-channel images from multiple conditions.
Adjust levels manually to obtain sharp resolution, monitoring histograms carefully.
Save “Look Up Table” (LUT) files for each channel using the “Save presets” function in the Levels pop-up window.
Apply LUT files as defined above to each single-channel image by the “Load presets” function in the Levels pop-up window.
Save level-optimized single-channel images in a dedicated folder for automated image analysis.
Identify nuclear objects as objects of 40–110 pixels diameter in blue-channel images using the “IdentifyPrimaryObjects” package.
Discard objects outside this diameter range and those on image borders.
Identify clumped objects by “Shape” and separate them based on “Signal intensity”.
Turn on additional features “Automatically calculate size of the smoothing filter for declumping” and “Automatically calculate minimal allowed distance between local maxima”.
Identify cellular objects with the “IdentifySecondaryObjects” package, expanding primary object by 50 pixels using the distance - N method.
Define cytoplasmic areas subtractively based on cellular and nuclear objects using the “IdentifyTertiaryObjects” package.
Discard objects outside a specified diameter range.
Discard objects located on image borders.
Identify clumped objects by their shape.
Separate clumped objects based on signal intensity.
Automatically calculate the size of the smoothing filter for declumping.
Calculate the minimal allowed distance between local maxima automatically.
Apply the “MeasureObjectIntensity” package to dsDNA+, COX4+, or TFAM+ objects.
Discard objects with a signal intensity less than 0.04.
Relate dsDNA+ objects and cytoplasmic areas as child and parent, respectively, using the “RelateObjects” package.
Using the “FilterObjects” package, select cytoplasmic areas containing a minimum value of 1 children object as positive cells.
Validate thresholds for each set of images using the "Test mode".
Interrogate quantitative data for number of cytosolic dsDNA+ dots per cell.
Determine percentage of cells exhibiting cytosolic dsDNA+ dots.
Relate dsDNA+ objects and nuclear objects as parent and child with the “RelateObjects” package.
Identify filtered dsDNA objects as nuclear by children category and nuclear count with a minimum value of 1.
Quantitative results and images exemplifying the analytic pathway can be exported in multiple file formats.
Interrogate quantitative data for percentage of dsDNA+ objects co-localizing with nuclear (DAPI+ or LMNB1+) objects over total dsDNA+ objects.
Relate dsDNA+ objects and COX4+ or TFAM+ objects as child and parent, respectively, using the “RelateObjects” package.
Filter results using 1 as a minimum measurement value using the “FilterObjects” package (COX4+ or TFAM+ objects that do not co-localize with dsDNA+ objects are excluded).
Interrogate quantitative data for percentage of dsDNA+ objects co-localizing with COX4+ or TFAM+ objects over total dsDNA+ objects.
